about: Passages labelled for thirteen rhetorical devices. Each item lists the devices present; every device not listed is labelled absent. split 'dev' items may be read while building the device readers; split 'heldout' items were written and labelled on 2026-10-26 before any reader existed and are scored only after the readers are frozen. One annotator labelled everything; a second annotator is an open step for the author. The dev items repeat the 49 passages of passages.json with a fuller label set (anaphora now also covers three clauses that open with one pronoun, so 'I came, I saw, I conquered' counts), plus new items for the added devices. Labels for isocolon and alliteration were tightened to the definitions above on 2026-10-26, before any reader was written or any item scored. A 'lookalike' item carries the surface shape of some device without that device; it may still carry other devices. On the same day, still before any held-out item was scored, anadiplosis was tightened to the first word of the next clause, and four items were relabelled to match their own definitions: c-draft-reads gains chiasmus; macbeth-fair-foul, c-test-ship and h-love-do gain anadiplosis. proverb-eat-live loses isocolon (3 and 5 words), also before held-out scoring. Split heldout-independent (80 items) was written on 2026-10-26 by a separate agent that saw only the definitions above, never the readers, the lexicons or the other items; it was merged after the reader source was frozen (sha256 of devices.py 8d59af09...). Split heldout was written by the reader builder before the readers existed, but the builder knew those items while writing the opposition lexicon, so it is not independent of the readers.

definitions.antithesis: two contrasting ideas set against each other in a balanced or mirrored construction, with or without a negation
definitions.tricolon: three parallel members used for rhythm or emphasis; a plain factual list of three items is not the device
definitions.anaphora: the same word or words repeated at the start of three or more successive clauses or sentences
definitions.chiasmus: two content words repeated in reverse order (A B, B A) across paired clauses
definitions.alliteration: three or more different words within six consecutive words that begin with the same consonant sound
definitions.assonance: three or more different stressed words within six consecutive words that share a vowel sound
definitions.polysyndeton: a series of three or more items or clauses with a conjunction before each item after the first
definitions.asyndeton: a series of three or more coordinate items or clauses with no conjunction
definitions.anadiplosis: the last content word of one clause repeated as the first word of the next, after at most a conjunction or an article
definitions.epizeuxis: a word repeated immediately, with at most a comma between, for emphasis
definitions.isocolon: two or more successive clauses, each with its own verb or a verb elided from a balanced pair, of near-equal length (within one word) and parallel structure; lists of single nouns or adjectives do not count
definitions.zeugma: one word, usually a verb, governing two others in different senses
definitions.oxymoron: two contradictory terms set side by side
